231.text: When you enter the monastery garden, you are taken aback: It won't be that easy to push your way through this undergrowth! Everything around you is overgrown - actually quite understandable, since nobody has taken care of this garden for decades. To put it bluntly (The gardener - if he's still alive - may forgive us...): This place looks more like a jungle than the carefully tended garden where, a long, long time ago, the monks of this monastery used to meditate! But as you brutally force your way through the thorny undergrowth, you suddenly come across a wrought-iron gate that at first glance was hidden by the undergrowth! As you look through the bars, you shudder: This is the gate that leads directly to the cemetery of the monastery, where all the dead of the village used to be buried! But something is wrong with this place: thick banks of mist creep sluggishly and ominously across the graveyard, but strangely do not penetrate the bars of the gate, but almost seem to be held back by a magical barrier. When you see that the mist seems to come straight out of the partly open and desecrated graves - almost as if the spirits of the dead wanted to flee their final resting place to take revenge on all living things - a chill runs down your spine. .. If you have the right key with you, you can enter the cemetery in the north - if you still have the courage to do so... If not, the small archway in the east will lead you back to the monastery.

Oh yes, indeed: it must be a really damn long time ago, because all the dining tables and benches are either broken on the floor or covered in rat droppings in such a way that you would hate to even touch them! Your impression gets stronger: this monastery has been deserted in a hurry - you're just wondering why... Exits lead in all directions except to the east.

233.text: You reach the throne room of Firon, king of the elves, unnoticed. Dazzled by the brilliant light reflected from the walls, you shield your eyes and look around in wonder. The hall is as empty as it is enormous. Its only 'furnishings' are Firon's ice throne and the glittering ice crystals hanging dozens of metres from the ceiling. They scatter the sunlight in every imaginable colour, as though carved from one gigantic, priceless gemstone...

234.text: Unfortunately, you decided to explore the frozen desert much deeper than was actually necessary. Well, blinded by the extremely bright sunlight, you unfortunately missed the crack in the ground directly in front of you - and stumbled straight into a deep glacier! Um, what more can I say about that? You should consider yourself lucky not to have starved to death, because entering this frozen wasteland without fast transportation is in itself certain death! But don't give up: Maybe one day you will be found and thawed out by a few scientists - younger and fresher than your peers will then be...

235.text: You continue your way through the cemetery, although you ask yourself with a rather unpleasant feeling in your stomach why everything around you has suddenly become so quiet... To the north, an ancient burial vault stands silhouetted against the sickly yellow light of the full moon, when the ominous silence is suddenly interrupted by a long, wild scream that makes your blood run cold: This scream was anything but human! But before you can think again, you hear a second - HUMAN - scream, which after a few seconds turns into a low whimpering, until it finally dies away completely... When you finally snap out of your paralysis, still shaking, you notice a hoarse hiss and the cracking of some branches behind you - and it's coming straight at you! So we should get these trembling legs moving and either seek refuge in the crypt in the north, or flee to the chapel in the eastern part of the cemetery!

236.text: With mixed feelings you enter the cemetery of the old monastery, while the gate in the southern wall squeaks terribly on its hinges - as if it were being moved by the freezing wind, which strangely seems to have picked up at the very moment you entered the cemetery. You shiver as you look down and see the billowing cold mist creeping up your legs. In the meantime it has become so foggy that you can hardly see the ground. Tentatively you put one foot after the other into this gray sea and follow the path towards the small chapel to the north, past weather-beaten tombstones and overturned wrought-iron crosses that seem to reach out to you in the eerie light like claws frozen in agony. .. -Hey, freak! Tell me, don't you actually have a watch, or are you blind? You're standing here in a cemetery, it's just after midnight - and WE HAVE A FULL MOON! If the rest of this game is as clichéd as the story so far suggests, something pretty bad is about to happen! Okay: if you're actually planning to take a little walk around here - please: nobody's holding you back - but please don't expect me to share your somewhat macabre hobbies with you! I'll wait here for you - MAYBE...! Oh, by the way: Have you already seen the open grave back there...?

237.text: This is - rather, WAS - the old monastery smithy, in which weapons, armor and objects of daily use were manufactured in the past. Many of the items are still lying around: for example, there are still some old, but still reasonably serviceable weapons hanging on the walls, and there is also an old anvil here, to which the smith's hammer has rusted fast over the years. The only way out of the forge is south, back into the monks' dining room.

238.text: You enter the king's burial vault. Hardly a ray of light falls through the small, barred hatch in the west wall. Right in the center of the tomb stands the king's mighty sarcophagus, adorned with scenes from his glorious exploits... The only way out of this dark and spooky room is through the door in the south wall, back to the moonlit graveyard...

239.text: You are standing in a small chapel, but in contrast to the rest of the monastery it is still quite well preserved. The large door in the south leads you back to the cemetery, while you can climb down the steps into the darkness. ..

240.text: This appears to be Mylgor's bedchamber. It really is by far the most tastefully furnished room in this house: an ornate bed stands against the north wall, with a small bedside table next to it. On the walls you can see some precious old oil paintings. The only exit is through the door in the east wall, back to the corridor...

241.text: You emerge into a short corridor, lit only by blazing torches on the black-painted walls. A massive steel door in the north wall bears the words 'Laboratory - Keep Out!' Iron rungs lead back up to Mylgor's fireplace room. You can try the laboratory to the north or the room to the west. Or, of course, you can climb the rungs back to the fireplace room above Mylgor's secret hideout...

242.text: As the sign on the door indicated, this is Mylgor's secret laboratory: it's overflowing with test tubes, flasks and measuring cups, filled with all sorts of mysterious liquids bubbling up in every imaginable color. You have to concentrate very hard in order not to be confused by this sudden flood of new impressions - but then you see him: MYLGOR, the malicious alchemist, the vassal of the great evil, whose name you don't even dare to utter in your mind! When your eyes meet, his face twists into a malicious grimace: he slowly approaches you, shows you an enormous veterinary syringe that he has just filled with a greenish, bubbling poison, and snarls: "You haven't been following my orders, my dear fellow, have you...?" You hastily look around for possible escape routes, but can't see anything apart from the huge steel door to the south...!

244.text: When the orc father happily sees his little son entering the cave behind you, his initially hostile gaze suddenly turns into a broad grin. "Oho! Looks as though we're having a guest for dinner!", he says, and you wince involuntarily - but he continues undeterred in his gruff manner, without even realizing the ambiguity of his words : "Well, if my wife should actually manage to grill the lizard before we all starve to death, you can have lunch with us. Just sit down - there's enough for all of us!" With very mixed feelings, you sit down on one of the small stools, trying frantically not to look at the animal over the fireplace...

245.text: While you wait for lunch, you and the orc father watch his little boy playing blissfully with the crystal ball you gave him. Suddenly it slips through his fingers! He leaps after it and chases it round the cave, squealing with delight, until a heroic dive finally catches it just short of the fireplace. Unfortunately, his hands close round the ball at exactly the moment he lands between his mother's feet. She is carrying the crockery to the table. She trips, and the whole lot crashes onto his back! Sitting in a mountain of broken crockery, the little orc starts bawling. At a curt, commanding glance from his father, his mother walks over and adds a hefty left hook to his troubles. That does it. Startled, he stops crying and looks round sheepishly... For a brief moment the whole family glares at the unhappy boy as he picks the last shards out of his fur. Nobody is paying any attention to you...

246.text: After you have entered the servants' room, Mylgor sticks his head through the door gap again, wishes you a good night's sleep, leaves the room - and locks the door behind him!

247.text: You hand the contract and knife back to the man. His face disappears from the hatch, and a few seconds later you hear the door being unlocked. "Come in!" He opens it and leads you into a small, cosy room with a fireplace. Introducing himself as "Mylgor, alchemist", he shows you where you will sleep. When you ask where he intends to sleep, he laughs heartily. "Do you really think a scientist like me could live in a hut this size? Good heavens, no! This is my servant's room. He is running errands for me in the next village. My laboratory and the other rooms are... hidden! Never mind where..." Mylgor nervously strokes his goatee, then forces that peculiar smile back onto his face. "But I thought we were going to talk about you, not me...?" He nods towards the fireplace room. "Let us chat by the fire for an hour. Perhaps I can tell you a little about our village's history. First, though, give me those wet things. You will catch your death!" Feeling distinctly uneasy, you undress while keeping a close eye on the old alchemist. What exactly is this favour you are supposed to do for him? Was that a greedy gleam in his eye? Just in case, you glance at your bedroom door. Thank goodness: it has a lock! Awkward and embarrassed, you hand Mylgor your clammy swimming trunks. All he does is lay them by the fire to dry...

248.text: When you enter the fireplace room again, you wonder why Mylgor actually didn't lock the door. Something in this house doesn't seem right - not at all right... You also wonder why Mylgor isn't there to greet you: maybe this is just a trap, because he has noticed that you didn't keep your promise to eliminate Firon? Or maybe King Richard and his brother didn't tell you the full truth and had Mylgor killed before you could see through them and right your mistake of letting Firon live? You have strong doubts and pangs of conscience when you consider that an innocent man may have died because of you...

249.text: In the middle of the clearing, a little orc boy is playing "ant bomber", a hunting game very popular among the orcs. He appears to be around eighty years old and not fully grown yet - but give it a few more centuries and he will easily strangle you with his left hand. You watch the child play for a few moments: his right hand hovers high in the air over an ant hole, while with his left he shoos the wood ants crawling around on the ground towards the hole. Every time an ant tries to slip into its burrow, the little one drops a pebble on it! However, the young orc doesn't seem to have had much luck in this game so far, you note with relief as he growls contritely in the face of an ant that he missed just before the hole: "Okay, 23:4 for you! But now you're in for it, lads!" At some point you get tired of watching the orc do his sadistic machinations and approach him. When he notices you, the little one hands you a few pebbles: "Here! Let's have a match: I'll bet two gold pieces!" Without accepting his offer, you take the pebbles from the boy's hand and forcefully throw them into the bushes. The orc seems to understand, pouts and mutters, "Fine. Don't, then..."

251.text: Throughout your long journey across the frozen wastes, you failed to notice the wolf pack following your sled's tracks. Now, as you stop to give your dogs a few minutes' rest, the wolves begin to circle you! The biggest, a huge beast with dirty grey fur, throws back its head and howls. A terrifying chorus joins in, as though a thousand throats were answering. These beasts can't have eaten in weeks. Without warning they attack the sled! Your dogs have run too far, and you've driven them too hard: they have no strength left to fight back. Helplessly, you watch the wolves tear them into a bloody mess. After ripping the entrails from the dogs' still-twitching bodies, the pack disappears as quickly as it arrived...

252.text: Heaven! It's probably already too late to even think about escaping: You have to watch, frozen in horror, as a huge, black shadow rises up behind a weather-beaten tombstone - only a few meters away from you! Unable to move, you have to watch as he silently grows bigger and bigger... Suddenly the cloud cover that had covered the full moon for a short time tears apart - and you scream out in panicky fear of death: Your opponent is a huge, gray werewolf baring his sharp yellow teeth in triumph! Hissing hoarsely and with outstretched arms, he starts moving - step by step, because he's in no hurry... But suddenly he stops! For fractions of a second, your eyes meet and you can feel the lust for murder and the abysmal hatred blazing in his eyes...

280.text: Before your undead opponent has a chance to attack, you strike his chest with one deft movement! However, just before your blade finds its target, you suddenly swing it upwards towards the beast's neck, where it leaves a gaping, smoking wound, without the werewolf having the slightest chance of warding off your murderously good blow! The undead creature, severely wounded by your sacred weapon, sinks to the ground with an incredulous look in its eyes and breathes out its "life". Your fear was unfounded: steaming, greenish blood is running from a long, gaping wound in his throat. Something else you also have to see is some red blood sticking to one of the wolf's claws - and as you examine yourself, plagued by forebodings, you can see a small, but still quite deep wound on your left leg, which the wolf must have torn while falling, and from which - GREEN blood is now seeping! CRAP! Now that you've noticed it, the wound starts to burn like hell: the infection has begun, and it will only be a matter of time before you too start to become a beast during the full moon! As you sit down in resignation on one of the fallen gravestones to ponder your uncertain fate, the wolf's body transforms into the decaying corpse of a once beautiful young woman who seems to look up at you gratefully! When you try to touch her - she turns to dust...

355.text: Firon replies, "To prove that I am on your side, I shall give you a key. Its purpose will become clear in time. I am not permitted to explain it myself, but there is someone... someone you should find in the old monastery on the hill in the northeast of the land. We both belonged to a group that secretly worked to address our country's troubles after evil gained the upper hand. Sadly..." He sighs, gazing past you for a moment into the cold emptiness. "Sadly, he did not manage to flee to us here in the frozen wastes. He fell into the hands of the evil one's hunters... I never saw him again, nor the monastery that had served as our secret headquarters. All I had left was a key. I cast a copy of it in magical ice and have kept it for decades. May it serve you well on your quest..." Firon rises, takes a large key from a hidden compartment in his throne and carefully places it in your outstretched hand. Glancing at the entrance behind you, he adds, "My guards will let you pass. I shall have one of my fastest badger sleds prepared to take you back to the edge of the frozen wastes. Farewell, my friend. May the gods protect you..." He beckons to the yeti, who escorts you outside to the waiting sled.

357.text: The king's ghost studies you for a while, then hops onto the edge of his coffin with a mischievous grin. Once comfortably seated, he begins the tale of his kingdom. "Long, long ago," he says, his face once again that of a bitter old man, "this was a beautiful, peaceful and prosperous land. I ruled my subjects wisely and justly from my castle on an island surrounded by crystal-clear water. Its magnificent buildings bore witness to my people's wealth and craftsmanship... At my court I employed a young magician named Zargon, who would entertain me with his tricks from time to time. He was gifted, remarkably so. Yet I never suspected that he occupied a secret chamber beneath my castle, where he conducted his magical experiments. He was obsessed with making gold, which he desperately needed to pay for lessons from the greatest magicians in the land. Eventually, his ambition was rewarded: he was admitted to the Seventh Circle of the Mages' Guild. His full magical power had awakened, and he was permitted to wield even the mightiest spells. In time he surpassed his former teachers, who watched their most gifted pupil's progress with growing concern. But his ambition knew no bounds. He wanted more. He wanted my throne! Rather than face my noble knights in honourable combat, he used his magic to raise an army of savage undead creatures... One dark night, with thunder and lightning raging as though Judgement Day had come, he gathered those hellish things outside my castle. As the tower clock struck midnight, the bodies of my ancestors rose from their coffins in the crypt beneath the royal chambers and opened the gates. What a cruel irony! Zargon and his henchmen overran the castle within minutes. None of us had expected such an attack. A fatal mistake... After breaking down my bedchamber door, Zargon's blackbloods dragged me before their master. Without a word of explanation or apology, he drove his rapier into my chest, right up to the hilt..."
